questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following about BRICS:
1. New Development Bank (NDB) is headquartered in Shanghai
2. BRICS was expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and UAE
3. Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) is BRICS' alternative to IMF
4. India holds the largest voting share in NDB
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - all 5 founding BRICS members have EQUAL voting share in NDB (each ~20%). No single country dominates. NDB HQ in Shanghai, first president from India (KV Kamath). CRA ($100 billion pool) provides liquidity support as IMF alternative. BRICS expansion (2024 Johannesburg summit) doubled membership.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
With reference to the QUAD (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue):
1. It comprises India, USA, Japan, and Australia
2. It has a formal military alliance treaty
3. It focuses on a 'Free and Open Indo-Pacific'
4. The Malabar Naval Exercise is a QUAD initiative
questions.explanation: 1 and 3 correct. Statement 2 WRONG - QUAD is NOT a formal military alliance (unlike NATO). It's a strategic dialogue/partnership with no mutual defense treaty. Statement 4 WRONG - Malabar Exercise predates QUAD (started 1992 as India-US bilateral; Japan joined 2015; Australia joined 2020). It's not officially a 'QUAD exercise' though all 4 participate now.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following about IMF Special Drawing Rights (SDRs):
1. SDR is an international reserve asset created by IMF
2. Its value is based on a basket of 5 currencies (USD, Euro, Yuan, Yen, Pound)
3. Countries can exchange SDRs for freely usable currencies
4. India's SDR quota determines its voting power in IMF
questions.explanation: All correct. SDR created 1969 as supplementary reserve asset. Basket: USD (43.38%), Euro (29.31%), Yuan (12.28%), Yen (7.59%), Pound (7.44%) - reviewed every 5 years. Yuan added 2016. SDRs are exchangeable for hard currencies. India's IMF quota (~2.7%) determines both voting power and SDR allocation. Quota reform has been pending to increase developing country representation.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
With reference to India's nuclear agreements and groups:
1. India is a member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG)
2. India has signed the CTBT (Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty)
3. India is a member of MTCR (Missile Technology Control Regime)
4. The 123 Agreement enabled Indo-US nuclear cooperation
questions.explanation: 3 and 4 correct. Statement 1 WRONG - India is NOT a member of NSG (membership blocked primarily by China). India has been seeking NSG membership since 2008 NSG waiver. Statement 2 WRONG - India has NOT signed CTBT (considers it discriminatory). India DID join MTCR (2016), Wassenaar Arrangement (2017), Australia Group (2018). 123 Agreement (2008) enabled civilian nuclear cooperation with US.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following about the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB):
1. It was proposed by China and is headquartered in Beijing
2. India is the second largest shareholder after China
3. USA and Japan are members of AIIB
4. It was established in 2016 as a multilateral development bank
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG - USA and Japan are NOT members of AIIB. They view it as China's attempt to counter the World Bank/ADB. India is 2nd largest shareholder (8.52% voting power) after China (26.6%). 100+ members. Focus: infrastructure development in Asia. India has received largest loans from AIIB. Established January 2016.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
With reference to the UN Security Council reform:
1. India seeks permanent membership with veto power
2. G4 nations (India, Germany, Japan, Brazil) collectively seek reform
3. The 'Coffee Club' opposes expansion of permanent members
4. Any UNSC reform requires ratification by all current P5 members
questions.explanation: All correct. India seeks permanent seat (ideally with veto, but has shown flexibility). G4 collectively push for expansion. Coffee Club (Uniting for Consensus: Italy, Pakistan, Mexico, South Korea etc.) opposes new permanent seats. Article 108 of UN Charter: any amendment needs 2/3 GA majority AND ratification by all P5 (US, UK, France, Russia, China) - giving each P5 effective veto over reform.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's Act East Policy:
1. It upgraded the earlier Look East Policy from economic to strategic engagement
2. India-ASEAN FTA covers only trade in goods, not services
3. India is a member of RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership)
4. The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway is a key connectivity project
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG - India WITHDREW from RCEP negotiations in 2019 (concerns about Chinese goods flooding Indian market, impact on domestic manufacturing/dairy/agriculture). India-ASEAN FTA in goods (2010) exists but services/investment agreement is limited. Trilateral Highway (India-Myanmar-Thailand, 1,400 km) and Kaladan Multi-Modal project are key connectivity initiatives.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
With reference to the International Solar Alliance (ISA):
1. It was jointly launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris
2. Its headquarters is in Gurugram, India
3. Membership is open only to countries between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn
4. It aims to mobilize $1 trillion for solar energy by 2030
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG - membership was INITIALLY limited to tropical countries, but after the ISA Framework Agreement amendment (2020), it is NOW open to ALL UN member states regardless of geographical location. HQ at National Institute of Solar Energy campus, Gurugram. 116+ member countries. India's major multilateral initiative in renewable energy diplomacy.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following about WTO:
1. Dispute Settlement Mechanism is often called the 'jewel in the crown' of WTO
2. India has successfully challenged developed countries in WTO disputes
3. The Appellate Body of WTO is currently non-functional
4. India's food stockholding for public distribution was challenged at WTO
questions.explanation: All correct. WTO Dispute Settlement is considered its most effective feature. India has won against US (solar cells), EU (IT tariffs). Appellate Body non-functional since Dec 2019 (US blocked appointments). India's MSP-based food procurement exceeded WTO's 10% subsidy limit under AoA - challenged by US/Australia. 'Peace Clause' (Bali 2013) provides interim protection until permanent solution found.

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
With reference to the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI):
1. It was proposed by India at the East Asia Summit 2019
2. It has 7 pillars including maritime security and trade connectivity
3. It is a military alliance against China
4. Australia is the lead partner for Maritime Ecology pillar
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG - IPOI is explicitly NOT a military alliance against any country. It's an open, inclusive initiative for cooperative engagement in the Indo-Pacific. 7 pillars: Maritime Security, Maritime Ecology, Maritime Resources, Capacity Building, Disaster Risk Reduction, Science & Technology, Trade Connectivity. Different countries lead different pillars.
